```{r}
#| label: index-setup
#| include: false
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)
library(here)

db_path <- here("cv-app-test", "cv.db")
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), db_path)

pub_count   <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM publications")$n
paper_count <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM papers_in_progress")$n
diss_count  <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM dissertation_committees")$n
svc_count   <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM academic_committees")$n

highlights <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT honorGrant, grantor, `where` AS location, year
  FROM honors_grants
  WHERE CAST(year AS INTEGER) >= 2022
  ORDER BY CAST(year AS INTEGER) DESC
")

dbDisconnect(con)
```

## About

John Paul Broussard is a Finance Professor with over 25 years of experience
spanning academic administration, international program development, applied
financial research, and classroom instruction.

His **administrative record** includes directing and co-directing graduate
finance programs at the University of Oklahoma — including the Online MS
Finance Program (150+ students, graduation rate above 78%, CFA Institute
University Affiliation) — and serving multiple terms as Finance Area Head
at Rutgers University and the Estonian Business School. He has led
curriculum redesign, faculty recruitment, strategic planning, and
development office engagement at institutions across three continents.

His **research** applies advanced quantitative methods to empirical finance.
Current work employs vine copula modeling, multimodal AI and NLP, and
network analysis to study central bank communication, endowment portfolio
management, commodity market dependence, financial influencer effects, and
the interaction of alternative and GAAP earnings. His work has appeared in
*Journal of Financial Economics*, *Management Science*, *European Financial
Management*, and 20 other peer-reviewed outlets.

His **international portfolio** spans sustained academic engagement in the
United States, Estonia, Finland, England, Switzerland, and Italy, including
a Fulbright Distinguished Chair in Business and Economics (Hanken School,
2016) and a Fulbright Finland Alumni Grant (2026).

His **teaching** integrates professional market standards with coursework.
As a CFA Charterholder, Certified Financial Risk Manager, and Professional
Risk Manager — and a trainer for both designation programs for nearly two
decades — he brings practitioner depth to every course, across in-person,
online, and international delivery formats.

## Recent Highlights

```{r}
#| label: recent-highlights
#| output: asis

if (nrow(highlights) > 0) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(highlights))) {
    h <- highlights[i, ]
    cat(sprintf(
      '<div class="honor-item%s">\n<div class="honor-year">%s</div>\n<div class="honor-content"><div class="honor-title">%s</div><div class="honor-org">%s · %s</div></div>\n</div>\n',
      if (h$year >= 2025) " major-honor" else "",
      h$year, h$honorGrant, h$grantor, h$location
    ))
  }
}
```

## Research Interests

Vine copula methods (D-vine / R-vine) in portfolio management and commodity
markets · Multimodal AI and NLP applied to central bank communication ·
Financial influencer network effects and retail investor behavior · Earnings
management and voluntary disclosure · Algorithmic trading and market
microstructure · Extreme value theory and risk measurement

[→ Working Papers](papers.qmd) · [→ Publications](research.qmd)

```{r}
#| label: footprint-map

institutions <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "Rutgers University (1997–Present)",
    "SUNY Empire State University (2025–Present)",
    "Estonian Business School (2018–2020; 2024–Present)",
    "ZHAW Banking & Finance (2024–Present)",
    "University of Oklahoma (2021–2024)",
    "Hanken School of Economics (2016–2020)",
    "University of Vaasa (collaborations)",
    "University of Oulu (collaborations)",
    "Turku School of Economics (visiting 2013)",
    "LUT University (visiting 2007)",
    "Middlesex University (2015–2016)",
    "Fairleigh Dickinson University (1995–1997)",
    "Louisiana State University (1992–1995)",
    "Millsaps College (1990–1991)",
    "Arezzo Study Abroad Program, Italy (2022–2024)",
    "University of New York Tirana (presentation)"
  ),
  lat = c(39.9483, 43.0668, 59.4370, 47.4979,
          35.2058, 60.1699, 63.0951, 65.0121,
          60.4518, 61.0589, 51.5893, 40.7587,
          30.4133, 32.3498, 43.4633, 41.3275),
  lng = c(-75.1210, -73.7863,  24.7536,  8.7280,
          -97.4395,  24.9384,  21.6165, 25.4651,
           22.2666,  28.1870,  -0.2292,-74.4171,
          -91.1800, -90.1848,  11.8800, 19.8187),
  status = c("current","current","current","current",
             "past","past","collab","collab",
             "visiting","visiting","past","past",
             "past","past","program","presentation"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

pal <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("#900000","#cc6666","#555555","#aaaaaa","#c0392b","#888888"),
  domain  = c("current","past","collab","visiting","program","presentation")
)

leaflet(institutions, width = "100%", height = "360px") |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lat = ~lat, lng = ~lng,
    color = ~pal(status),
    radius = ~ifelse(status == "current", 10, 7),
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    stroke = TRUE, weight = 1.5,
    popup = ~paste0("<strong>", name, "</strong>")
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = c("#900000","#cc6666","#c0392b","#555555","#aaaaaa","#888888"),
    labels = c("Current","Past","Program","Collaboration","Visiting","Presentation"),
    title = "Affiliation type", opacity = 0.85
  )
```
